name: PA-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of about eight points on the PVI
Incumbent Madeleine Dean running with a large cash advantage of $1.2 million on hand
Prediction markets price Dean at roughly 97% to win
No general-election polling available, leaving the forecast dependent on fundamentals
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Dean: an eight-point Democratic district, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising edge against a little-known challenger with no visible resources. Markets agree, pricing her near 97%, so the race stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any late surge in outside spending against Dean or unexpected polling showing a much tighter race would be the main signal to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Madeleine Dean seeks another term in a suburban Philadelphia district that leans about eight points Democratic at the baseline. She is a well-established incumbent who has raised roughly $1.4 million and holds about $1.2 million on hand, while Republican challenger Aurora Stuski reports no significant fundraising or outside support. No independent groups have spent against Dean.

No public general-election polls are available for this race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and market pricing. Prediction markets put Dean's win probability near 97%. The combination of a favorable district, incumbency, and a large resource gap makes an upset unlikely, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
